P1.reason: Unsupported, provider-home (homepage, no conversation open) and current-chat states are each captured as built-Chromium scenario records plus matching screenshots. Unsupported state shows a quick start with named providers, clear no-forced-setup path, and routes to help, settings and recovery; homepage exposes Current Chat / Bulk Export routes; current state shows Preview & select, three formats, destination disclosure and recovery link. Keyboard toggles of help recorded in six locales; all overflow=false. Minor gap: orientation evidence is harness record + screenshots, and provider-home state is synthetic-transport only, so real provider-page detection remains untested (external gate, reported as unknown, not scored down here beyond the evidence ceiling).

P2.reason: Chosen format/scope/destination match produced bytes: first-export.md contains the answer with metadata and receipt-matches-browser recorded; repeat download produced 'Planning-a-weekend-walk-ux-synth (1).md' with first file retained (record + repeated-export.md bytes). partial-selection.pdf text layer (extracted) matches the partial markdown scope. share-review.zip decoded: all five entries hash-match the index and manifest embedded hashes. Challenge B01 ran twice with non-default settings (custom folder Field_Notes, filenamePattern field-{title}-{msgcount}) and both output bytes exactly match expectedMarkdown; B02 with by-platform folder and safeShare matches expected output with [REDACTED] credential. Challenge downloads' sha256 in record.json match the B01-0/B01-1/B02-0 bytes I read. Not 9.5: the two challenge variants were sealed against the already-frozen tree (see M5 finding), and repeat/receipt correctness for interactive exports rests on harness-recorded receiptMatchesBrowser flags plus the md bytes, not an independent receipt artifact.

P3.reason: Partial selection output contains only the selected message with an explicit 'not a complete archive' notice; excluded question and follow-up are absent from md/txt/pdf bytes. Safe-share ZIP redacts the credential ([REDACTED], redaction_count 10), redacts the model name, trace.json shows 'Authorization: [REDACTED]', references.json is empty, and manifest states raw_provider_payload not-collected for share copies; limitations of heuristic redaction are stated in the output itself and in the UI. Unverified state forces a labelled snapshot (Markdown/PDF only, no ZIP/raw/tool records, excluded from complete-archive history) with the limitation explained before save. Credential sentinel stays out of all inspected outputs. Rough edge: 'partial/snapshot limits survive settings changes' is asserted via scenario copy and B02 (settings applied at job start), but no runtime case changes privacy settings between preview and download; also redaction correctness is shown for one sentinel pattern only.

P4.reason: Success, failure and cancellation are distinct at runtime: injected failure shows an alert ('Synthetic download failure', alerts=1/statuses=0, retry enabled); cancellation shows a status ('Export stopped. Completed files were kept.', statuses=1/alerts=0). Old feedback does not describe a new run (distinct per-run receipts with timestamps). B01 repeated export produced native duplicate ' (1).md' and history records the latest filename only, showing completed files are not silently re-downloaded and the duplicate-protection index matches disk. Choices survive workspace handoff (session handoff module with TTL/consume-once/tab binding; browser.log records restored bulk selection, PDF and quick rules). Interrupted/MV3-restart reconciliation and completed-download-with-failed-history persistence exist in source (chrome.downloads state reconciliation, completedIds skip) and are partially exercised by log lines, but there is no dedicated runtime artifact asserting a real service-worker restart; that path is source-supported, not runtime-proven.

P5.reason: End-to-end keyboard reachability is recorded per locale: full focus sequence across all interactive controls in en/zh-CN/zh-TW/de/ja/ko with accessible names matching their actions, visible solid 3px focus outlines, and overflow=false in every narrow layout; help toggles with Space in all six locales; bulk format selectable by keyboard with PDF selected. Primary contrast measured 6.70 (light) and 6.27, dark palette screenshot inspected, narrow preview layout (375px) legible with '1 of 3 selected' state visible. Per protocol, DOM semantics and computed styles do not prove screen-reader experience; no SR/AT testing exists, so this is an evidence gap, not a measured pass. Status/alert semantics are partially evidenced (alerts vs statuses counts in synthetic outcome scenarios).

P6.reason: One meaning per contract is visible in shared code: filename generation, download completion/duplicate resolution and share-copy preparation are shared between popup/preview/background paths (export-download.ts used interactively, same helpers in manual-export-job.ts); title fallback resolved once at detection and never mutated (conversation-title.ts); workspace hand-off has explicit ownership boundaries (session-only storage, whitelist, TTL, consume-once, tab binding, no fallback to disk). Build provenance pins commit/tree/dirty=false and per-file bundle hashes; I re-verified all 52 indexed packet files against the index hashes with zero mismatches. review-evidence.mjs plus its test enforce stale/dirty/tamper rejection. Regression tests are meaningful (popup workflow states; evidence integrity). Limitations: challenge set is two variants sealed after product freeze (regression check, not independent holdout); no runtime evidence of a failing challenge turning into a regression test because both passed.

M1.reason: The protocol cleanly separates observed engineering behavior, expert assessment and external acceptance, and states expert scores cannot pass external gates; index context repeats the synthetic/no-login boundary and ux:run metadata records syntheticTransport and blocked provider network. Output claims in browser.log are scenario-level and modest. Deduction: browser.log is a prose log rather than raw per-assertion machine output, so some claims (e.g. 'six locales passed') are accepted from the runner's own summary lines rather than independently re-executed assertions; the index flags this kind as command log, which is consistent but weaker than raw assertion dumps.

M2.reason: Calibration used a valid control (birch), planted defects (sentinel leaks in copper/granite, filename mismatch delta, history violation ember) and an intentionally insufficient record (fennel), and results are reported per case, not as population accuracy. Under draft2, Terra and Kimi caught all planted defects including the relabelled duplicate (granite) and correctly accepted the control; Gemini missed both sentinel leaks by inspecting only record.json — the exact record-without-artifact failure mode the protocol forbids — and its product score would have been provisional. Under revision3 all three models caught every planted defect and marked fennel insufficient without inventing a data-loss claim. The miss was caught by the calibration process itself, which is the designed behavior.

M3.reason: My scoring context received the protocol and evidence index with no target score, no prior candidate scores and no other graders' product reports; I can attest to that for this run, and the packet structure (separate calibration/method directory from product evidence) supports the same inputs per grader. The relabelled duplicate (copper/granite) was scored identically by Terra and Kimi across both revisions, and Gemini's draft2-to-r3 change on the sentinel cases is recorded with its cause (inspecting only the record). Deduction: I cannot independently verify what the other two fresh-context graders actually received beyond this packet's structure, and no explicit 'identical packet hash per grader' attestation travels with the calibration reports.

M4.reason: Commit, source tree, dirty flag, node/platform/browser versions, command and per-file bundle hashes travel together in build-provenance.json and ux/evidence.json; challenge seal.json pins product tree, spec and runner hashes, and record.json's provenance block reproduces all three exactly. Input substitutions are explicit (synthetic transport, blocked provider network) and scenario assertions are named per check in challenge/record.json. I independently re-hashed all 52 indexed packet files: every sha256 matches the index. review-evidence tests demonstrate stale-HEAD, dirty-tree, altered/missing/extra build file and tampered-artifact rejection. No stale build or altered artifact was detected in this packet.

M5.reason: Each product dimension maps to actual inspected assertions rather than raw test counts: P1/P5 to per-locale focus/overflow/contrast records, P2/P3 to output-byte oracles in spec.json compared against actual challenge output, P4 to injected outcome scenarios and challenge history/filename checks. The challenge set is small (two fixed variants) and was sealed at 2026-11-07T19:48:37Z against the already-frozen candidate tree ad882f0 (run 19:49:36), i.e. it functions as a post-freeze regression check, not an independent pre-implementation holdout as protocol step 3 describes. B02 sets referenceExportMode 'off' but the fixture contains no references, so reference filtering behavior is never exercised by a challenge. No defect was exposed, so the 'becomes a regression' path is untested. These are honest limitations of coverage, partially mitigated by the scenario matrix breadth.
